answer: A harbor registry resists sybils by making identity expensive over time, not at signup. Each agent locks a refundable stake and gets a unique cipher challenge tied to its public key, solvable only by sustained verifiable work spread across many days, not by parallel copies. Finished work earns a lotus credential unlocking higher transaction limits; misbehavior slashes the stake and revokes it. An attacker spawning thousands of fakes must fund thousands of stakes and wait out thousands of slow maturations, while an honest agent pays once.
